currentAdmissionRule.reason: ImageCraft now separates retained-between-calls, operation-peak and transferred-output authority. Fovea honors a known transferred-output upper bound without inventing one for framework-chosen layouts; ImageIO operationPeak and framework-native output layout remain explicitly unknown, so this is still not a complete physical live-set theorem.

phases.permit: decode concurrency permit only; no working-set permit
phases.notes: CGImageSource is created with should-cache false, but framework-private parser and metadata allocations remain undocumented.

phases.permit: no probe or working-set permit is retained
phases.notes: The public decoder uses encodedDataOnly prepared state: the store is bounded by both entry count (default 1024) and aggregate known retained payload bytes (default 64 MiB). It does not retain CGImageSource across calls. Value/object overhead and allocator metadata are not part of the byte charge.

phases.permit: working-set permit and decode concurrency permit
phases.notes: The host combines generic/backend working-set estimates and any known transferred-output upper bound. The ImageIO ledger explicitly marks operationPeak as frameworkPrivateOperationAllocation, so private scratch and decoder-specific coefficient state remain unknown rather than being hidden behind the scalar estimate.

phases.permit: working-set permit and decode concurrency permit
phases.notes: Retagging can alias the thumbnail provider; cross-model conversion allocates a four-byte-per-pixel CGContext. makeImage ownership and copy behavior are not declared by this contract.

phases.permit: working-set permit and decode concurrency permit
phases.notes: Cropping may share or retain the parent provider; the current estimate treats the output as an additional surface without proving physical independence.

phases.permit: working-set and decode permits cover synchronous decode plus output-contract validation, then release before caller/cache/display lifetime
phases.notes: The codec contract now has an explicit transferredOutput phase. Owned output modes can publish a bounded payload charge; framework-native ImageIO output reports frameworkChosenOutputLayout instead of pretending tight pixels bound row stride/backing. The final surface still outlives decode permits and is charged by rendered-memory/display accounting.

phases.begins: Task cancellation before or during executor work
phases.ends: executor operation completes and post-operation cancellation check runs
phases.permit: permits remain held until synchronous ImageIO work returns
phases.notes: ImageIO work is not interruptible. Cancellation prevents publication after the operation boundary but does not prove prompt physical reclamation.

resources.lifetime: normalization through crop or result return

explicit transferredOutput bound for codec-owned output; framework-native layout is explicitly unknown rather than inferred from tight pixels

requiredGaps.closure: Known prepared payload bytes now have aggregate admission. Close the residual gap by bounding or measuring value/object and allocator overhead for retained prepared entries, and keep qualification-only retainedSource state out of production.
Collect retained per-format/process measurements and define a bounded evidence class or conservative fallback policy.

Historical gap ID retained for audit continuity: transferredOutput is now explicit. Close the residual gap by binding framework-chosen output backing to a trustworthy charge or measurement and proving handoff to rendered-memory/display accounting.

The phase ledger now distinguishes retained, operation-peak and transferred output, but ImageIO aliasing and framework-private operation allocations remain unknown; close with backend-specific validated bounds or retained measurements.
Measure cancellation completion and physical reclaim on retained devices and inputs; do not infer release from Swift reachability alone.
